narrative.overview:
Magpipe is a dark, quiet enclosure in which a few bright birds are always visible. The ground is near-black and stays that way; the only light on it is the white of the things you can act on (the logo on its disc, the primary button, the live dot) and one sheen — cyan running to teal and emerald — that marks what is alive, current or identifying (eyebrows, the active underline, the wing, a glow around a running thing). Everything else is drawn with hairlines so the birds carry the picture.

The surface is an operator's tool, so familiarity is a feature: one sans for everything, mono where numbers and identifiers live, fixed sizes rather than fluid ones, a stable top nav. Brand shows in precise details — the gradient-clipped eyebrow, the cyan hairline under the frosted nav, mono fact lines, the magpie — never in decoration. Copy is short and plain; the bird metaphor is allowed in headings and prose and kept out of any label that must be precise. There is no light theme and no second accent: green, purple and blue as UI colours are rejected.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas with a faint dot grid and one ambient cyan glow; depth from hairlines, not shadows.
White is the only solid accent; the cyan→teal→emerald sheen appears only as a signal.
Inter at fixed sizes, light display weights, mono for data; eyebrows in tracked uppercase.
Small radii (6–8 px), pills only for status and filters, 1 px hairlines, 2 px active underline.
Motion is a state, not a texture: a pulsing dot, a glow on hover, nothing on page load.

rules.name: The White Acts Rule
rules.body: White fills nothing that cannot be pressed. The primary button, the logo disc and the live dot are white; a decorative white surface is a mistake.

rules.name: The Sheen Signals Rule
rules.body: Cyan, teal and emerald never fill a control or a panel. They appear as text (eyebrows), as a 1–2 px line (active underline, hover border, nav hairline), as a glow on a live or hovered thing, and as the wing. Their rarity is what makes "running" legible.

rules.name: The Two Semantics Rule
rules.body: Amber means "needs you", red means "failed". No other colour carries meaning; status otherwise reads from a word, a dot and position.

rules.name: The Measured Column Rule
rules.body: Prose widths are set in rem, not ch — Inter is narrower than its zero, so ch overshoots the 65–75 character measure.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the operator might copy or compare — an id, a count, a token total, a model name, a path — is set in the mono stack, often in Mute.

rules.name: The Light as State Rule
rules.body: Nothing glows at rest except the one primary action and the orb. Glow means "live", "hovered" or "press me"; a decorative glow is a lapse.

dos: Do make white mean action: primary buttons, the disc, the live dot — nothing decorative.
Do keep the sheen to lines, text, glows and the wing; signal, never fill.
Do set ids, counts, models and paths in mono, usually Mute, often select-all.
Do give every disabled control a visible reason, every empty state a real next step, and every error its remedy.
Do hold prose to ≈72 characters with rem widths (34 rem at 16 px, 31 rem at 14 px).
Do opt motion in with motion-safe:; keep state transitions at 150 ms.
donts: Don't introduce a light theme, a blue, a purple or any second accent.
Don't add drop shadows at rest or glow anything that is not live, hovered or the primary action.
Don't use the bird metaphor in status pills, fact lines, table cells or Settings rows.
Don't nest cards, widen radii past 8 px (pills excepted), or use ch for measure.
Don't let gradient text appear anywhere but the eyebrow; a single short eyebrow word renders solid.
